## PR Checklist
Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#commit
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)


## PR Type
What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [x] Bugfix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.io application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:


## What is the current behavior?
<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Issue Number: #36259
Several pipes have incomplete or incorrect typing.

## What is the new behavior?
The common pipes should now all have a stricter typing.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [X] Yes
- [x] No

<!-- If this PR contains a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->

It depends on what is considered a breaking change: some code that would compile will now trigger a compilation error. On the other hand, the code that is made invalid by this change, such as passing an object to a numeric pipe, was incorrect in the first place (it caused errors at runtime instead of at compile time).

Fixing the fallout should be trivial.

## Other information
Originally posted as https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/36277

issue_context.title: add Promise<T> | Observable<T> async pipe overload
issue_context.body:
# 🚀 feature request

### Relevant Package
`@angular/common`

### Description
Currently the async pipe can take a Promise or Observable, but only as seperate obverloads, so with `strictTemplates` you get an error if you pass in a `Promise<T> | Observable<T>`

### Describe the solution you'd like
Add an overload which looks like `transform<T>(obj: Promise<T> | Observable<T> | null | undefined): T | null;`


### Describe alternatives you've considered
converting the promise into a observable, but this isn't ergonomic


Happy to submit a patch

nit: I think this is fine to keep as is, just change the return type to be `value is null|undefined`. Alternatively, you could use the [nullish coalescing](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-3-7.html#nullish-coalescing) operator to get rid of this method entirely.

I would rather avoid the `value is null|undefined` route, as the signature would be very misleading: value could also be `''` (which could be added to the signature) or `NaN` (which cannot be expressed as a literal type).

It is not clear to me how to use the `??` to get rid of this function... wouldn't you still need to check for `''` and `NaN` at every location?
Could we also support `ReadonlyMap` here?

Yes :)
That has already been changed in https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/37311 and will stay like that when these changes are rebased

Prefer strict equality

```suggestion
    if (value === null || value === undefined) return null;
```

it's a nit but it makes the intention clearer IMO
Right now all of the (common) pipes that work on scalar values check for `== null`. Should I change it also in the other ones?
didn’t realize it was a convention, disregard
sure! :) should I go forward with that?

In a way, it looks like a good idea, as it provides a type-level "documentation" of the behavior in these special cases.
OTOH, it looks like a strange commitment from the perspective of the API
:+1: love that the cast can be dropped here

Shouldn't this be
```suggestion
      input: Record<K, V>, compareFn?: (a: KeyValue<number, V>, b: KeyValue<number, V>) => number):
```

Which makes it equivalent to the next overload with `K extends string|number`.

no, the `keyvalue` pipe passes the `number` keys as strings in the case of a `Record<number, V>` object :(

I tried to explain it in the commit message, but maybe it is not explicit enough (and maybe we should also add a comment in the code to explain it, so it does not get lost in the git history)
Oh, I see. I didn't originally read the commit message; it may indeed be a good idea to include a comment in the code to mention this is intentional.

Do we not prefer use of `isNaN`?

```suggestion
  return !(value == null || value === '' || isNaN(value));
```
TypeScript rejects it because `value` is typed as `number|string` at that point.

I think this signature is not technically required, as its return type is `string|null` just like the third signature and the ordering doesn't matter in this case (i.e. this signature can be moved one down without changing the matching behavior, and can then be merged with the 3rd signature). I don't particularly mind, and from a docs perspective it may seem weird that the primary signature only takes `null|undefined`, so I am fine with keeping as is.

This comment also applies to some other pipes below.
I agree it is not really needed but it makes the overload options clearer to the user of the code.

Removing it also makes the pipe very weird when applied to `any`, as in that case TypeScript uses the first overload (since any overload matches `any`) instead of the most generic one.

This is very inconvenient when the first overload handles "special" cases (`null | undefined`) as it causes the result to be typed `null` as well
